hypotheses.title: Multinational Foreign Currency Translation Risk Management and 1-Year Average Yield
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Multinational companies reporting higher gains on foreign currency transactions and tax translation adjustments (fn_oth_income_loss_fx_transaction_and_tax_translation_adj_a / _q) possess superior treasury risk management and currency hedging capabilities. Observing average gains over a 1-year horizon filters out transient currency shocks, isolating persistent balance-sheet strength and operational hedging resilience. Subindustry neutralization removes macro currency beta, while quadratic power conviction and short-term reversal overlays optimize turnover and Sharpe.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if foreign exchange translation gains stem entirely from unhedged speculative currency swings rather than disciplined risk management.

candidates.rationale: Candidate 1: 1-Year Trailing Average FX Translation Gain normalized by Market Cap (FX Earnings Yield) with Reversal Stabilizer
Candidate 2: 1-Year Time-Series Percentile of Asset-Normalized FX Translation Gain with Reversal Stabilizer
Candidate 3: Trailing 4-Quarter (1-Year) Rolling Average of Quarterly FX Translation Gains normalized by Assets with Reversal Stabilizer
